case.summary: Customer C07297 reported a $482.12 online purchase as unauthorized. Investigation revealed four rapid online purchases totaling $1,906.07 within 30 minutes on November 21, 2016, each structured just under the $500 authorization threshold, executed from two distinct device profiles across two billing regions. This pattern precisely matches five prior confirmed fraud cases, indicating compromised card used for organized fraudulent transactions. Verdict: confirmed fraud (probability 0.9, Policy R9). Actions taken: card blocked, case created, regulatory report filed, escalated to analyst.

sar.narrative: On November 21, 2016, between 20:00 and 20:30, card C07297-K1 (customer C07297) was used for four rapid online purchases: $478.95, $456.96, $488.04, and $482.12, totaling $1,906.07 in exposure. Customer C07297 reported the final transaction ($482.12, transaction ID 3476682 at 20:30) as not authorized by the cardholder. Each transaction amount was deliberately structured to remain just below the $500 authorization threshold, suggesting an attempt to evade detection controls. The purchases originated from two distinct device profiles—one using Windows 7 with Internet Explorer 11.0 (1920×1080 resolution) and another using iOS 11.2.1 with Mobile Safari (2208×1242 resolution)—and were processed through two different billing regions (264.0 and 476.0). This pattern of structured sub-$500 transactions combined with rapid, coordinated use from multiple device profiles indicates card compromise and organized fraudulent activity. Notably, an identical structuring pattern appears in five prior closed cases (CC-3748, CC-3841, CC-3907, CC-4086, CC-4124), suggesting systematic targeting of compromised cards by an organized fraud ring. Per Policy R9 (undocumented coordinated patterns), the card has been blocked, an investigation case has been created, and the matter has been escalated to an analyst for review of connected accounts and device profiles.

stop_reason: Pattern matched confirmed closed cases and the cardholder denial settled the verdict; further queries would not change the actions.
